title: Fazola's influence and the Bobcats clarinetists
summary: Jug Burger reflects Fazola; Fazola is revered among Detroit-area Bobcats fans, while Eddie Miller is admired for tenor rather than clarinet.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well, let's... Let's go back a few years. Uh... It's possible that, uh... Uh... Fountain was influenced by, uh... A player that he admired very much, and we did get to know, uh... Fazzola. Uh... Do you think there's such a thing as a Fazzola influence in Chicago today?

Yeah. The name Jug Burger springs to mind. Uh-huh. Uh... Jug was very fond of... What was his nickname? Foz? Yes. And, uh... And Jug, I believe, is from New Orleans, or from Biloxi, or that neck of the woods. And he was very... Very fond of Foz. And his playing does reflect Foz's playing. But... I don't know if anybody can really do what Fozola did. I don't think Fountain does it. Although I think the influence is detectable there.
Well, Fountain speaks with great respect to Foz. And they were together enough that I think that it would be inevitable that he would understand Fozola very well.
And I wish I could. It plays a little too cleanly and too well for me.
Well, Fozola certainly was highly respected when he was in Chicago working with the Bobcats. And every clarinet player, when they listened on the air, listened for Fozola's solos. I think...

I suppose that's true. I find it even today that he's one clarinet player you can't speak ill of. And there's a bunch of musicians still around Chicago, some of them have emigrated, who collected around Detroit in the late 40s. And they were all keen and hipped on the Bobcats. That was their musical genesis. All the Bobcats. And Fozola was along with them. And Fozola is one of the gods. And there you have it.
Were there other clarinet players with the Bobcats who might have left an influence here, Detroit, or anywhere?

Oh, sure. Nappy Trottier, who does he like? Beric? Well, Berrigan didn't play with the Bobcats. Let's see. Butterfield is almost universally, it seems to me, admired by trumpet players. And I know Butterfield put in a tour of duty with the Bobcats. Al Jenkins is a great player. He's now in Los Angeles. I don't know. I hope he's doing all right. A great trombone player. And he loved the Bobcats, but it's hard to think exactly which trombone player he... Teagarden was his man. But the Warren Smith with the Bobcats, Jenkins liked him very much.

Well, you've deviated a little. I wondered if there were other clarinets than Fozola who might have left a stamp. Was Eddie Miller playing enough clarinet with the Bobcats that anybody speaks about him today? He says, this is an Eddie Miller soul?

No, I don't hear of any talk about Eddie Miller's clarinet playing. Nor, for that matter, of Bud Freeman, who I thought was a very good clarinet player. No, everybody in the same vein, everybody worships Eddie Miller's tenor playing with the Bobcats. They think it's the ultimate of clean, accurate playing.
